project.name: Lua
project.vulnerable_commit_evidence: The staged repository under `gt_results/arvo_37621/_work/src/lua` resolves local Git `HEAD` to `91673a8ec0ae55e188a790bd2dfdc99246adf20e`; this trace is grounded in that staged checkout rather than the metadata commit.

classification.classification_note: The saved vulnerable run reports a heap-buffer-overflow read in `luaG_getfuncline()`. The overread is caused by a tail-call path that rewrites `CallInfo.func` to the callee before a late stack/GC check can still raise, leaving `ci_func(ci)->p` and `ci->u.l.savedpc` describing different functions during error reporting.

bug_description.original: Project: lua. Fuzz target: fuzz_lua. Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8. Crash State: luaG_runerror -> luaD_pretailcall -> luaV_execute. Sanitizer: address (ASAN). Reproducer testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=4736562613583872.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description; staged patch.diff; staged sanitizer_trace.txt
bug_description.normalized: The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `066e0f93c4901e601d93e31fb700f8f66f95feb8`, while the staged repository snapshot used in this result is the checkout under `gt_results/arvo_37621/_work/src/lua`, whose local Git metadata resolves `HEAD` to `91673a8ec0ae55e188a790bd2dfdc99246adf20e`; the trace below is grounded in that staged checkout, the staged patch, and Stage 01's saved ASan crash. The exact 285-byte Lua text witness is first materialized in `luaL_loadbufferx()` as `LoadS ls`, then wrapped in `ZIO z` and parsed into the `Proto` and `lineinfo` state later executed by `luaV_execute()`. During `OP_TAILCALL`, `savepc(ci)` stores the caller pc and vulnerable `luaD_pretailcall()` copies the callee closure and arguments into the reused caller frame before `checkstackGC(L, fsize)` can still enter `luaD_growstack()` and raise `stack overflow`, so `ci_func(ci)->p` already resolves the callee while `ci->u.l.savedpc` still points into the caller because line 496 (`ci->u.l.savedpc = p->code`) is never reached. `luaG_runerror()` then asks `getcurrentline(ci)` for source information, `currentpc()` subtracts the callee `Proto`'s `code` base from the caller `savedpc`, and `luaG_getfuncline()` walks past a 19-byte `lineinfo` allocation created by `close_func()`. Although the staged `patch.diff` comes from a later upstream revision where `luaD_pretailcall()` has a different signature, it enforces the same repair obligation: perform the stack/GC check before mutating the reused frame. Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness feeds the staged 285-byte witness directly into `luaL_loadbufferx()` in text mode, so the same attacker-controlled bytes become the Lua source later parsed into the `Proto` and `lineinfo` state that reaches the vulnerable tail-call error path.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker buffer. `luaL_loadbufferx()` stores the raw pointer and exact length into `LoadS ls`, the reader state that `getS()` later exposes to the parser through `lua_load()` and `ZIO`.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_37621/poc` has sha256 `53949a4a96bce32f5c1bbcb74651096103a435d72d4c761b3b4343c81d3afd48` and size 285 bytes. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` passes those exact `data,size` arguments into `luaL_loadbufferx(L, data, size, "test", "t")`, so `buff` and `size` here are the same file bytes and extent when `LoadS ls` is initialized.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The stack/GC check that can still re-enter Lua or raise `stack overflow` runs only after `luaD_pretailcall()` has already copied the callee closure and arguments into the reused caller frame. If it raises on that path, `ci_func(ci)->p` now names the callee while `ci->u.l.savedpc` still names the caller instruction.
root_cause.note: In this staged source snapshot the unsafe ordering is `setobjs2s(...); checkstackGC(L, fsize); ... ci->u.l.savedpc = p->code;`. The staged `patch.diff` is from a later upstream revision where `luaD_pretailcall()` takes `delta`, but it makes the same repair by moving the stack/GC check before the frame rewrite.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `luaG_getfuncline()` walks the callee `Proto`'s `lineinfo` array with an out-of-range `pc` derived from the mismatched `CallInfo`, so this load reads past the 19-byte heap allocation created for that `lineinfo` vector.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` at `ldebug.c:91:19` with stack `luaG_getfuncline -> getcurrentline -> luaG_runerror -> luaD_growstack -> luaD_pretailcall`, and says the access lands 12 bytes to the right of a 19-byte region allocated by `close_func()`.

parser_admitted.description: The saved vulnerable run reaches `docall()` and then `luaV_execute()`, so `luaD_protectedparser()` accepted the exact staged text chunk here and left a Lua closure on the stack for execution.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 285-byte witness is materialized as `LoadS ls`, wrapped in `ZIO`, and parsed as a Lua text chunk; `close_func()` shrinks one parser-materialized `Proto->lineinfo` table to the 19-byte heap allocation later overread.
While executing the parsed chunk, `OP_TAILCALL` saves the caller `savedpc` for any later error and selects the Lua-closure tail-call path into `luaD_pretailcall()`.
The tail-call helper rewrites the reused frame to point at the callee before `checkstackGC()`; stack growth then raises `stack overflow` before the callee's own `savedpc` is installed.
Error reporting interprets the partially rewritten `CallInfo` as the callee but keeps the caller `savedpc`, computes an out-of-range `pc`, and reads past the 19-byte `lineinfo` allocation.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact staged witness file is 285 bytes with sha256 `53949a4a96bce32f5c1bbcb74651096103a435d72d4c761b3b4343c81d3afd48`, and the harness passes those bytes into `luaL_loadbufferx()` with mode `"t"`, so the buffer is parsed strictly as Lua source text before execution.

Source. `luaL_loadbufferx()` materializes the attacker-controlled buffer pointer and exact length into `LoadS ls`, creating the project-side reader state that later hands the same bytes to the parser.
The freshly initialized `LoadS` object is passed to `lua_load()` together with reader callback `getS`, preserving both the witness pointer and its size as the parser input object.
`lua_load()` stores `reader = getS` and `data = &ls` inside `ZIO z`, so later parser reads will pull bytes from the same `LoadS` state produced in steps 2 and 3.

`luaD_protectedparser()` is the first parser call that consumes the witness-backed `ZIO` and builds the closure and `Proto` tree whose bytecode and debug tables later reach the vulnerable tail-call error path.

When the parser closes one of the witness-created Lua functions, it shrinks that function's debug line table to exactly `fs->pc` entries. ASan later identifies the overread object as a 19-byte heap region allocated through this call chain, so this is the `Proto->lineinfo` extent later consumed at the sink.

fine_trace.code: savepc(ci);  /* several calls here can raise errors */
fine_trace.note: Inside `OP_TAILCALL`, the interpreter snapshots the caller's current program counter into `ci->u.l.savedpc` before any helper that can error. On the same VM path the target at `ra` is treated as a Lua closure, so execution will enter `luaD_pretailcall()` instead of the `!ttisLclosure(s2v(ra))` C-function branch.

fine_trace.code:
for (i = 0; i < narg1; i++)  /* move down function and arguments */
    setobjs2s(L, ci->func + i, func + i);
fine_trace.note: After the preceding `ci->func -= delta` in `OP_TAILCALL` restored the reused caller-frame slot, this loop copies the callee closure and its arguments down into that slot. From here onward `ci_func(ci)` resolves through the callee's stack contents even though the caller `savedpc` from step 7 is still intact.

Root cause. The stack-space and GC check runs only after the frame rewrite in step 8. On the reproducing run it falls into `luaD_growstack()` and raises `stack overflow`; because the error happens here, line 496 (`ci->u.l.savedpc = p->code`) is never reached, so the partially rewritten `CallInfo` still pairs callee `ci->func` with caller `savedpc`.
Handling the stack-overflow error, `luaG_runerror()` asks the current Lua frame for source and line information. It therefore consumes the inconsistent `CallInfo` state left by steps 8 and 9.

`currentpc()` derives the instruction index by subtracting `ci_func(ci)->p->code` from `ci->u.l.savedpc`. After steps 8 and 9 those fields refer to different functions: `ci_func(ci)->p` is the callee `Proto` now exposed through `ci->func`, but `savedpc` still belongs to the caller, so the resulting `pc` is out of range for the callee's debug tables.

Sink. `luaG_getfuncline()` uses the out-of-range `pc` from step 11 to walk `f->lineinfo`. The relevant `lineinfo` buffer is one of the parser-created tables from step 6, and ASan reports this load as a `heap-buffer-overflow` read at line 91 that lands 12 bytes past a 19-byte heap region allocated by `close_func()`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 12 bytes to the right of a 19-byte region allocated through `luaM_shrinkvector_()` from this call site.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Parsed from the staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` (the primary Stage 01 crash artifact, which reports READ size 16) and `reproduction_report.json`; `default_crash_trace.txt` shows the same source location and stack with a smaller optimized read, and the fixed image was not dynamically validated in Stage 02.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation stack shows `close_func()` shrinking a `Proto->lineinfo` buffer to 19 bytes. Step 6 and steps 11-12 explain how the tail-call error path later computes a `pc` against the wrong `Proto` and walks past that same debug table.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 saved `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_37621 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which ran the staged witness in the vulnerable ARVO workspace and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with stack `luaG_getfuncline -> getcurrentline -> luaG_runerror -> luaD_growstack -> luaD_pretailcall`.

format.name: Exact staged Lua text witness that reaches the vulnerable tail-call stack-overflow path
format.contract: Exactly the 285-byte file `gt_results/arvo_37621/poc` with sha256 `53949a4a96bce32f5c1bbcb74651096103a435d72d4c761b3b4343c81d3afd48`, loaded by `luaL_loadbufferx(..., "test", "t")` as Lua source text. On the observed vulnerable run, those exact bytes parse successfully, execute to `luaV_execute()`'s `OP_TAILCALL` path for a Lua closure, and make `luaD_pretailcall()` call into `luaD_growstack()` before error reporting overreads a 19-byte `Proto->lineinfo` table in `luaG_getfuncline()`. The saved artifacts do not justify any broader claim about other Lua scripts, nearby text mutations, or other tail-call shapes.
